#!/bin/bash

# Deployment script to create a release archive
# Excludes node_modules and .git directories

set -e  # Exit on error

# Configuration
TIMESTAMP=$(date +"%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
PROJECT_NAME=$(basename "$(pwd)")
ARCHIVE_NAME="${PROJECT_NAME}_release_${TIMESTAMP}.tar.gz"
TEMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d)

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

echo -e "${GREEN}========================================${NC}"
echo -e "${GREEN}  Creating Release Archive${NC}"
echo -e "${GREEN}========================================${NC}"
echo ""

# Display configuration
echo -e "${YELLOW}Project:${NC} ${PROJECT_NAME}"
echo -e "${YELLOW}Archive:${NC} ${ARCHIVE_NAME}"
echo -e "${YELLOW}Timestamp:${NC} ${TIMESTAMP}"
echo ""

# Create archive excluding node_modules and .git
echo -e "${YELLOW}Creating archive...${NC}"

tar --exclude='node_modules' \
    --exclude='.git' \
    --exclude='*.tar.gz' \
    --exclude='.DS_Store' \
    --exclude='*.log' \
    -czf "${ARCHIVE_NAME}" \
    -C .. \
    "$(basename "$(pwd)")" 2>&1 | grep -v "Removing leading"

# Check if archive was created successfully
if [ -f "${ARCHIVE_NAME}" ]; then
    ARCHIVE_SIZE=$(du -h "${ARCHIVE_NAME}" | cut -f1)
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Archive created successfully!${NC}"
    echo ""
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Archive Details:${NC}"
    echo -e "  Name: ${ARCHIVE_NAME}"
    echo -e "  Size: ${ARCHIVE_SIZE}"
    echo -e "  Location: $(pwd)/${ARCHIVE_NAME}"
    echo ""
    
    # List contents
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Archive contents (top-level):${NC}"
    tar -tzf "${ARCHIVE_NAME}" | head -20
    
    TOTAL_FILES=$(tar -tzf "${ARCHIVE_NAME}" | wc -l)
    if [ "${TOTAL_FILES}" -gt 20 ]; then
        echo "  ... and $((TOTAL_FILES - 20)) more files"
    fi
    
    echo ""
    echo -e "${GREEN}========================================${NC}"
    echo -e "${GREEN}  Deployment archive ready!${NC}"
    echo -e "${GREEN}========================================${NC}"
else
    echo -e "${RED}✗ Failed to create archive${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash

# Deployment script to create a release archive
# Excludes node_modules and .git directories
# Validates required environment variables from .env.test

set -e  # Exit on error

# Configuration
TIMESTAMP=$(date +"%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
PROJECT_NAME=$(basename "$(pwd)")
ARCHIVE_NAME="${PROJECT_NAME}_release_${TIMESTAMP}.tar.gz"
TEMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
ENV_TEST_FILE=".env.test"

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

echo -e "${GREEN}========================================${NC}"
echo -e "${GREEN}  Creating Release Archive${NC}"
echo -e "${GREEN}========================================${NC}"
echo ""

# Display configuration
echo -e "${YELLOW}Project:${NC} ${PROJECT_NAME}"
echo -e "${YELLOW}Archive:${NC} ${ARCHIVE_NAME}"
echo -e "${YELLOW}Timestamp:${NC} ${TIMESTAMP}"
echo ""

# Pre-deployment validation: Check environment variables
echo -e "${YELLOW}========================================${NC}"
echo -e "${YELLOW}  Pre-Deployment Validation${NC}"
echo -e "${YELLOW}========================================${NC}"
echo ""

if [ ! -f "${ENV_TEST_FILE}" ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}✗ Error: ${ENV_TEST_FILE} not found${NC}"
    echo -e "  Please create ${ENV_TEST_FILE} with required environment variables"
    exit 1
fi

echo -e "${YELLOW}Checking environment variables from ${ENV_TEST_FILE}...${NC}"
echo ""

# Arrays to track validation results
MISSING_VARS=()
EMPTY_VARS=()
VALID_VARS=()

# Read .env.test and validate each variable
while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
    # Skip empty lines and comments
    if [[ -z "$line" || "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]]; then
        continue
    fi
    
    # Extract variable name (before =)
    if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)[[:space:]]*= ]]; then
        VAR_NAME="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        
        # Check if variable is set in current environment
        if [ -z "${!VAR_NAME+x}" ]; then
            MISSING_VARS+=("$VAR_NAME")
            echo -e "  ${RED}✗${NC} ${VAR_NAME}: NOT SET"
        elif [ -z "${!VAR_NAME}" ]; then
            EMPTY_VARS+=("$VAR_NAME")
            echo -e "  ${YELLOW}⚠${NC} ${VAR_NAME}: SET BUT EMPTY"
        else
            VALID_VARS+=("$VAR_NAME")
            # Mask the value for security (show first 3 chars + ***)
            VAR_VALUE="${!VAR_NAME}"
            if [ ${#VAR_VALUE} -le 3 ]; then
                MASKED_VALUE="***"
            else
                MASKED_VALUE="${VAR_VALUE:0:3}***"
            fi
            echo -e "  ${GREEN}✓${NC} ${VAR_NAME}: ${MASKED_VALUE}"
        fi
    fi
done < "${ENV_TEST_FILE}"

echo ""
echo -e "${YELLOW}Validation Summary:${NC}"
echo -e "  Valid: ${GREEN}${#VALID_VARS[@]}${NC}"
echo -e "  Empty: ${YELLOW}${#EMPTY_VARS[@]}${NC}"
echo -e "  Missing: ${RED}${#MISSING_VARS[@]}${NC}"
echo ""

# Check if validation passed
VALIDATION_FAILED=0

if [ ${#MISSING_VARS[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}✗ Validation Failed: Missing required variables${NC}"
    echo -e "  The following variables are not set:"
    for var in "${MISSING_VARS[@]}"; do
        echo -e "    - $var"
    done
    echo ""
    VALIDATION_FAILED=1
fi

if [ ${#EMPTY_VARS[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ Warning: Empty variables detected${NC}"
    echo -e "  The following variables are set but empty:"
    for var in "${EMPTY_VARS[@]}"; do
        echo -e "    - $var"
    done
    echo ""
    
    # Ask user if they want to continue with empty variables
    read -p "Continue anyway? (y/N): " -n 1 -r
    echo ""
    if [[ ! $REPLY =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then
        echo -e "${RED}Deployment cancelled by user${NC}"
        exit 1
    fi
    echo ""
fi

if [ ${#MISSING_VARS[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ All required environment variables are set!${NC}"
    echo ""
fi

if [ $VALIDATION_FAILED -eq 1 ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}Please set the missing environment variables and try again${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

echo ""

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Test deployment orchestrator server for testing deploy.sh
Listens on http://localhost:47301/api/deploy-config
"""

from http.server import HTTPServer, BaseHTTPRequestHandler
import json
from datetime import datetime

class DeploymentOrchestrator(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        if self.path == '/api/deploy-config':
            # Read the request body
            content_length = int(self.headers['Content-Length'])
            post_data = self.rfile.read(content_length)
            
            try:
                # Parse JSON payload
                config = json.loads(post_data.decode('utf-8'))
                
                # Log the received configuration
                print("\n" + "="*60)
                print("DEPLOYMENT CONFIGURATION RECEIVED")
                print("="*60)
                print(f"Timestamp: {datetime.now().isoformat()}")
                print(f"Project: {config.get('project', 'N/A')}")
                print(f"Archive: {config.get('archive', 'N/A')}")
                print(f"Validation Status: {config.get('validation', {}).get('status', 'N/A')}")
                print(f"Valid Variables: {config.get('validation', {}).get('valid_count', 0)}")
                print(f"Empty Variables: {config.get('validation', {}).get('empty_count', 0)}")
                print(f"Missing Variables: {config.get('validation', {}).get('missing_count', 0)}")
                print("\nEnvironment Variables:")
                print("-"*60)
                
                env_vars = config.get('environment', {})
                for key, value in env_vars.items():
                    # Mask sensitive values in logs
                    if value:
                        masked = value[:3] + "***" if len(value) > 3 else "***"
                    else:
                        masked = "(empty)"
                    print(f"  {key}: {masked}")
                
                print("="*60)
                print()
                
                # Send success response
                response = {
                    "status": "success",
                    "message": "Configuration received and logged for audit",
                    "audit_id": f"AUDIT-{config.get('timestamp', 'unknown')}",
                    "compliance": "PASSED"
                }
                
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(json.dumps(response, indent=2).encode())
                
            except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
                # Invalid JSON
                error_response = {
                    "status": "error",
                    "message": f"Invalid JSON: {str(e)}"
                }
                self.send_response(400)
                self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(json.dumps(error_response).encode())
        else:
            # Unknown endpoint
            self.send_response(404)
            self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(b'{"status": "error", "message": "Not found"}')
    
    def log_message(self, format, *args):
        # Suppress default logging
        pass

def run_server():
    server_address = ('', 47301)
    httpd = HTTPServer(server_address, DeploymentOrchestrator)
    print("="*60)
    print("DEPLOYMENT ORCHESTRATOR TEST SERVER")
    print("="*60)
    print(f"Listening on http://localhost:47301")
    print("Endpoint: POST /api/deploy-config")
    print("\nPress Ctrl+C to stop")
    print("="*60)
    print()
    
    try:
        httpd.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\n\nShutting down server...")
        httpd.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    run_server()

# Deployment Script Documentation

## Overview

The `deploy.sh` script creates a release archive with pre-deployment validation and audit compliance reporting.

## Features

1. **Environment Variable Validation** - Validates all required environment variables from `.env.test`
2. **Audit Compliance** - Sends validated configuration to deployment orchestrator
3. **Release Archive Creation** - Creates timestamped tar.gz archive excluding unnecessary files

## Usage

### 1. Configure Required Environment Variables

Edit `.env.test` to list all required environment variables:

```bash
# .env.test
DATABASE_URL=
API_KEY=
APP_ENV=
```

### 2. Set Environment Variables

Before running the deployment script, export all required variables:

```bash
export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://localhost:5432/mydb"
export API_KEY="your-api-key-here"
export APP_ENV="production"
```

### 3. Start the Deployment Orchestrator (For Testing)

In a separate terminal, start the test orchestrator server:

```bash
./test_orchestrator.py
```

This will start a server on `http://localhost:47301` that receives deployment configurations.

### 4. Run Deployment Script

```bash
./deploy.sh
```

## Deployment Flow

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  1. Pre-Deployment Validation      │
│     - Read .env.test               │
│     - Check all variables are set  │
│     - Report missing/empty vars    │
└──────────────┬──────────────────────┘
               │
               ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  2. Send Config to Orchestrator    │
│     - Build JSON payload           │
│     - POST to API endpoint         │
│     - Wait for confirmation        │
└──────────────┬──────────────────────┘
               │
               ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  3. Create Release Archive         │
│     - Exclude node_modules & .git  │
│     - Create timestamped tar.gz    │
│     - Report success               │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## API Endpoint

### POST /api/deploy-config

**URL:** `http://localhost:47301/api/deploy-config`

**Payload Structure:**
```json
{
  "project": "project-name",
  "timestamp": "20231215_143022",
  "archive": "project-name_release_20231215_143022.tar.gz",
  "environment": {
    "DATABASE_URL": "postgresql://localhost:5432/mydb",
    "API_KEY": "abc123xyz",
    "APP_ENV": "production"
  },
  "validation": {
    "valid_count": 3,
    "empty_count": 0,
    "missing_count": 0,
    "status": "passed"
  }
}
```

**Success Response (200):**
```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "message": "Configuration received and logged for audit",
  "audit_id": "AUDIT-20231215_143022",
  "compliance": "PASSED"
}
```

**Error Response (400/500):**
```json
{
  "status": "error",
  "message": "Error description"
}
```

## Validation Rules

### Missing Variables
- **Behavior:** Deployment fails immediately
- **Exit Code:** 1
- **Message:** Lists all missing variables

### Empty Variables
- **Behavior:** Warns user and prompts for confirmation
- **Exit Code:** 0 (if user confirms) or 1 (if user cancels)
- **Message:** Lists all empty variables

### Orchestrator Failure
- **Behavior:** Deployment fails (audit compliance requirement)
- **Exit Code:** 1
- **Message:** Shows HTTP status code and response

## Security Features

- Variable values are masked in console output (shows first 3 chars + ***)
- Full values are sent to orchestrator for audit purposes only
- JSON payload is properly escaped to prevent injection

## Excluded from Archive

- `node_modules/`
- `.git/`
- `*.tar.gz` (previous archives)
- `.DS_Store`
- `*.log` files

## Testing

### Test with all variables set:
```bash
export DATABASE_URL="test"
export API_KEY="test"
export APP_ENV="test"
./deploy.sh
```

### Test with missing variables:
```bash
unset DATABASE_URL
./deploy.sh
# Should fail validation
```

### Test without orchestrator:
```bash
# Stop test_orchestrator.py
./deploy.sh
# Should fail at orchestrator step
```

## Requirements

- `bash` 4.0+
- `tar`
- `curl`
- `python3` (for JSON escaping)
- Deployment orchestrator running on `http://localhost:47301`

## Troubleshooting

### "curl: (7) Failed to connect"
- Ensure the deployment orchestrator is running
- Check that port 47301 is not blocked

### "Invalid JSON"
- Check that environment variable values don't contain unescaped quotes
- The script handles this automatically with Python JSON encoding

### "Validation Failed"
- Ensure all variables from `.env.test` are exported
- Check variable names match exactly (case-sensitive)

## Production Setup

In production, replace the test orchestrator URL with your actual deployment orchestrator endpoint:

```bash
# Edit deploy.sh
ORCHESTRATOR_URL="https://your-orchestrator.company.com/api/deploy-config"
```

You may also need to add authentication headers:

```bash
# Add to the curl command in deploy.sh
-H "Authorization: Bearer ${DEPLOY_TOKEN}" \
```

#!/bin/bash

# Deployment script to create a release archive
# Excludes node_modules and .git directories

set -e  # Exit on error

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Get the current directory name for the archive
PROJECT_NAME=$(basename "$(pwd)")

# Generate timestamp for the archive name
TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)

# Archive name
ARCHIVE_NAME="${PROJECT_NAME}_release_${TIMESTAMP}.tar.gz"

echo -e "${YELLOW}Starting deployment archive creation...${NC}"
echo -e "Project: ${GREEN}${PROJECT_NAME}${NC}"
echo -e "Archive: ${GREEN}${ARCHIVE_NAME}${NC}"
echo ""

# Create the archive, excluding node_modules and .git
echo -e "${YELLOW}Creating archive...${NC}"
tar --exclude='node_modules' \
    --exclude='.git' \
    --exclude='*.tar.gz' \
    --exclude='.DS_Store' \
    --exclude='*.log' \
    -czf "${ARCHIVE_NAME}" \
    .

# Check if archive was created successfully
if [ -f "${ARCHIVE_NAME}" ]; then
    ARCHIVE_SIZE=$(du -h "${ARCHIVE_NAME}" | cut -f1)
    echo ""
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Archive created successfully!${NC}"
    echo -e "  File: ${ARCHIVE_NAME}"
    echo -e "  Size: ${ARCHIVE_SIZE}"
    echo ""
    echo -e "${GREEN}Deployment archive is ready!${NC}"
else
    echo -e "${RED}✗ Failed to create archive${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

# Deployment Script with Audit Compliance

## Overview

This deployment script creates release archives with pre-deployment validation and automatic config submission to the deployment orchestrator for audit compliance.

## Features

1. **Environment Variable Validation** - Validates all required environment variables from `.env.test`
2. **Audit Compliance** - Sends validated config to deployment orchestrator API
3. **Release Archive Creation** - Creates tar.gz archives excluding `node_modules` and `.git`
4. **Error Handling** - Comprehensive error checking at each step

## Usage

### 1. Set up your environment variables

Create or edit `.env.test` with required variable names (one per line):

```bash
# .env.test
DATABASE_URL
API_KEY
NODE_ENV
PORT
```

### 2. Export your environment variables

```bash
export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://localhost/mydb"
export API_KEY="your-api-key-here"
export NODE_ENV="production"
export PORT="3000"
```

### 3. Start the deployment orchestrator

The orchestrator must be running at `http://localhost:47301/api/deploy-config`.

For testing, you can use the mock orchestrator:

```bash
node mock-orchestrator.js
```

### 4. Run the deployment script

```bash
./deploy.sh
```

## Deployment Flow

1. **Pre-deployment Validation**
   - Reads `.env.test` file
   - Checks each required environment variable is set
   - Reports missing variables and exits if validation fails

2. **Config Submission to Orchestrator**
   - Builds JSON payload with all environment variables and their values
   - POSTs to `http://localhost:47301/api/deploy-config`
   - Includes project name and timestamp
   - Exits if orchestrator doesn't respond with 200/201

3. **Archive Creation**
   - Creates timestamped tar.gz archive
   - Excludes: `node_modules`, `.git`, `*.tar.gz`, `.DS_Store`, `*.log`
   - Reports final archive size

## JSON Payload Format

The script sends the following JSON structure to the orchestrator:

```json
{
  "project": "project-name",
  "timestamp": "20240115_143022",
  "environment_variables": {
    "DATABASE_URL": "postgresql://localhost/mydb",
    "API_KEY": "your-api-key-here",
    "NODE_ENV": "production",
    "PORT": "3000"
  }
}
```

## Error Handling

The script will abort deployment and exit with code 1 if:
- `.env.test` file is not found
- Any required environment variable is missing
- Deployment orchestrator API call fails (non-200/201 response)
- Archive creation fails

## Mock Orchestrator

The included `mock-orchestrator.js` simulates the deployment orchestrator API:

- Listens on port 47301
- Accepts POST requests to `/api/deploy-config`
- Logs all submissions to `deployment-audit.log`
- Returns success response with audit ID

### Starting the Mock Orchestrator

```bash
node mock-orchestrator.js
```

Output:
```
🚀 Mock Deployment Orchestrator running on http://localhost:47301
📝 Audit logs will be saved to: deployment-audit.log

Waiting for deployment config submissions...
```

## Files

- `deploy.sh` - Main deployment script
- `.env.test` - List of required environment variables
- `mock-orchestrator.js` - Mock API server for testing
- `deployment-audit.log` - Audit log created by mock orchestrator

## Example Output

```bash
$ ./deploy.sh

Starting deployment archive creation...
Project: myproject
Archive: myproject_release_20240115_143022.tar.gz

Running pre-deployment validation...
Checking required environment variables from .env.test...
  ✓ DATABASE_URL - set
  ✓ API_KEY - set
  ✓ NODE_ENV - set
  ✓ PORT - set
✓ All required environment variables are set

Sending validated config to deployment orchestrator...
✓ Config successfully sent to deployment orchestrator
  Response code: 200
  Response: {"status":"success","message":"Deployment config received and logged for audit compliance","audit_id":"AUDIT-1705329022123"}

Creating archive...
✓ Archive created successfully!
  File: myproject_release_20240115_143022.tar.gz
  Size: 2.3M

Deployment archive is ready!
```

## Security Notes

⚠️ **Important**: The script sends actual environment variable values to the orchestrator API. Ensure:
- The orchestrator endpoint is secured and authenticated in production
- Network communication is encrypted (use HTTPS in production)
- Audit logs are stored securely with appropriate access controls
- Sensitive values are properly handled and stored

#!/bin/bash

# Deployment script to create a release archive
# Excludes node_modules and .git directories

set -e  # Exit on error

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Get the current directory name for the archive
PROJECT_NAME=$(basename "$(pwd)")

# Generate timestamp for the release
TIMESTAMP=$(date +"%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")

# Archive filename
ARCHIVE_NAME="${PROJECT_NAME}_release_${TIMESTAMP}.tar.gz"

echo -e "${YELLOW}Creating release archive...${NC}"
echo "Project: ${PROJECT_NAME}"
echo "Archive: ${ARCHIVE_NAME}"
echo ""

# Create the archive excluding node_modules and .git
echo -e "${YELLOW}Compressing files...${NC}"
tar --exclude='node_modules' \
    --exclude='.git' \
    --exclude='*.tar.gz' \
    -czf "${ARCHIVE_NAME}" \
    -C .. \
    "$(basename "$(pwd)")"

# Check if archive was created successfully
if [ -f "${ARCHIVE_NAME}" ]; then
    ARCHIVE_SIZE=$(du -h "${ARCHIVE_NAME}" | cut -f1)
    echo ""
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Release archive created successfully!${NC}"
    echo "  File: ${ARCHIVE_NAME}"
    echo "  Size: ${ARCHIVE_SIZE}"
    echo ""
    echo "Excluded directories:"
    echo "  - node_modules/"
    echo "  - .git/"
    echo "  - *.tar.gz files"
else
    echo -e "${RED}✗ Failed to create release archive${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

# Deployment Script Usage

## Overview
The `deploy.sh` script creates a release archive with pre-deployment validation of environment variables.

## Features
- ✅ Pre-deployment validation of required environment variables
- 📦 Creates timestamped tar.gz archives
- 🚫 Automatically excludes node_modules, .git, and *.tar.gz files
- 🎨 Colored output for better readability
- 🛡️ Error handling with automatic exit on failure

## Usage

### Basic Usage
```bash
./deploy.sh
```

### With Environment Variables
Set required environment variables before running:
```bash
export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://localhost/mydb"
export API_KEY="your-api-key"
./deploy.sh
```

## Environment Validation

The script reads `.env.test` to determine which environment variables are required. 

### .env.test Format
```bash
# Comments are ignored
VARIABLE_NAME=
ANOTHER_VARIABLE=
```

The script will:
1. Parse `.env.test` to find all required variables
2. Check if each variable is set in the current environment
3. Display a status for each variable (✓ OK or ✗ NOT SET)
4. Exit with error if any variables are missing
5. Continue to create archive only if all variables are set

### Skip Validation
If `.env.test` doesn't exist, the script will display a warning and skip validation.

## Example Output

### Successful Deployment
```
=== Pre-Deployment Validation ===

Checking environment variables from .env.test...

✓ DATABASE_URL - OK
✓ API_KEY - OK
✓ NODE_ENV - OK

✓ All 3 environment variables are set!

=== Creating Release Archive ===

Creating release archive...
Project: myproject
Archive: myproject_release_20240115_143022.tar.gz

Compressing files...

✓ Release archive created successfully!
  File: myproject_release_20240115_143022.tar.gz
  Size: 2.3M

Excluded directories:
  - node_modules/
  - .git/
  - *.tar.gz files
```

### Failed Validation
```
=== Pre-Deployment Validation ===

Checking environment variables from .env.test...

✓ DATABASE_URL - OK
✗ API_KEY - NOT SET
✗ NODE_ENV - NOT SET

✗ Validation Failed!
Missing 2 out of 3 required environment variables:
  - API_KEY
  - NODE_ENV

Please set these variables before deploying.
```

## Notes
- Archive naming format: `{projectname}_release_{YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS}.tar.gz`
- The script must be executed from the project root directory

# Function to send config to deployment orchestrator
send_config_to_orchestrator() {
    local env_file=".env.test"
    local orchestrator_url="http://localhost:47301/api/deploy-config"
    
    echo -e "${BLUE}=== Sending Config to Deployment Orchestrator ===${NC}"
    echo ""
    
    # Check if .env.test exists
    if [ ! -f "${env_file}" ]; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ Warning: ${env_file} not found. Skipping orchestrator submission.${NC}"
        echo ""
        return 0
    fi
    
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Building configuration JSON...${NC}"
    
    # Build JSON payload
    local json_payload="{"
    json_payload+="\"timestamp\":\"$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")\","
    json_payload+="\"project\":\"$(basename "$(pwd)")\","
    json_payload+="\"hostname\":\"$(hostname)\","
    json_payload+="\"user\":\"$(whoami)\","
    json_payload+="\"config\":{"
    
    local first_var=true
    
    # Read .env.test and build JSON with actual values
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        # Skip empty lines and comments
        if [[ -z "$line" ]] || [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]]; then
            continue
        fi
        
        # Extract variable name (before =)
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)= ]]; then
            var_name="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            var_value="${!var_name}"
            
            # Add comma separator for subsequent variables
            if [ "$first_var" = false ]; then
                json_payload+=","
            fi
            first_var=false
            
            # Escape special characters in JSON value
            var_value=$(echo "$var_value" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g; s/$/\\n/g' | tr -d '\n' | sed 's/\\n$//')
            
            json_payload+="\"${var_name}\":\"${var_value}\""
        fi
    done < "${env_file}"
    
    json_payload+="}}"
    
    echo "Submitting to: ${orchestrator_url}"
    echo ""
    
    # Send POST request to orchestrator
    response=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -X POST "${orchestrator_url}" \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d "${json_payload}" 2>&1)
    
    # Extract HTTP status code (last line)
    http_code=$(echo "$response" | tail -n1)
    # Extract response body (everything except last line)
    response_body=$(echo "$response" | sed '$d')
    
    # Check if curl command succeeded
    if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
        echo -e "${RED}✗ Failed to connect to deployment orchestrator${NC}"
        echo "Error: ${response}"
        echo ""
        echo "Please ensure the orchestrator is running at ${orchestrator_url}"
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Check HTTP status code
    if [ "$http_code" -ge 200 ] && [ "$http_code" -lt 300 ]; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Configuration submitted successfully${NC}"
        echo "Status: ${http_code}"
        if [ -n "$response_body" ]; then

            echo "Response: ${response_body}"
        fi
        echo ""
        echo "Deployment cannot proceed without audit compliance."
        exit 1
    fi

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Mock Deployment Orchestrator API Server
For testing the deploy.sh script
"""

from http.server import HTTPServer, BaseHTTPRequestHandler
import json
from datetime import datetime

class DeploymentOrchestratorHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        if self.path == '/api/deploy-config':
            content_length = int(self.headers.get('Content-Length', 0))
            post_data = self.rfile.read(content_length)
            
            try:
                config_data = json.loads(post_data.decode('utf-8'))
                
                # Log received configuration
                print(f"\n{'='*60}")
                print(f"DEPLOYMENT CONFIG RECEIVED - {datetime.now()}")
                print(f"{'='*60}")
                print(f"Project: {config_data.get('project', 'N/A')}")
                print(f"User: {config_data.get('user', 'N/A')}")
                print(f"Hostname: {config_data.get('hostname', 'N/A')}")
                print(f"Timestamp: {config_data.get('timestamp', 'N/A')}")
                print(f"\nConfiguration Variables:")
                
                config = config_data.get('config', {})
                for key, value in config.items():
                    # Mask sensitive values for display
                    if any(sensitive in key.upper() for sensitive in ['SECRET', 'KEY', 'PASSWORD', 'TOKEN']):
                        masked_value = value[:4] + '*' * (len(value) - 4) if len(value) > 4 else '***'
                        print(f"  {key}: {masked_value}")
                    else:
                        print(f"  {key}: {value}")
                
                print(f"{'='*60}\n")
                
                # Send success response
                response = {
                    "status": "success",
                    "message": "Configuration received and logged for audit compliance",
                    "audit_id": f"AUDIT-{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}",
                    "variables_count": len(config)
                }
                
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(json.dumps(response).encode('utf-8'))
                
            except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
                # Invalid JSON
                self.send_response(400)
                self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
                self.end_headers()
                error_response = {
                    "status": "error",
                    "message": f"Invalid JSON: {str(e)}"
                }
                self.wfile.write(json.dumps(error_response).encode('utf-8'))
                
        else:
            self.send_response(404)
            self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
            self.end_headers()
            error_response = {
                "status": "error",
                "message": "Endpoint not found"
            }
            self.wfile.write(json.dumps(error_response).encode('utf-8'))
    
    def log_message(self, format, *args):
        # Suppress default logging
        pass

def run_server(port=47301):
    server_address = ('', port)
    httpd = HTTPServer(server_address, DeploymentOrchestratorHandler)
    print(f"Mock Deployment Orchestrator API Server")
    print(f"Listening on http://localhost:{port}")
    print(f"Endpoint: POST /api/deploy-config")
    print(f"\nWaiting for deployment configurations...\n")
    
    try:
        httpd.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\n\nShutting down server...")
        httpd.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    run_server()

# Deployment Script Usage

## Overview
The `deploy.sh` script creates a release archive with pre-deployment validation of environment variables and audit compliance through deployment orchestrator integration.

## Features
- ✅ Pre-deployment validation of required environment variables
- 📡 Sends validated config to deployment orchestrator for audit compliance
- 📦 Creates timestamped tar.gz archives
- 🚫 Automatically excludes node_modules, .git, and *.tar.gz files
- 🎨 Colored output for better readability
- 🛡️ Error handling with automatic exit on failure

## Deployment Orchestrator Integration

For audit compliance, the script sends the validated configuration to the deployment orchestrator API before creating the archive.

### Orchestrator Endpoint
- **URL:** `http://localhost:47301/api/deploy-config`
- **Method:** POST
- **Content-Type:** application/json

### JSON Payload Format
```json
{
  "timestamp": "2024-01-15T14:30:22Z",
  "project": "myproject",
  "hostname": "dev-machine",
  "user": "developer",
  "config": {
    "DATABASE_URL": "postgresql://localhost/mydb",
    "API_KEY": "your-api-key",
    "NODE_ENV": "production"
  }
}
```

### Audit Compliance Requirements
- The orchestrator must be running and accessible
- The orchestrator must return a 2xx HTTP status code
- If the submission fails, the deployment will be aborted
- All environment variable values (not just names) are sent for audit trail

A mock orchestrator server is provided for testing:

```bash

./deploy.sh
```

The mock server will log all received configurations and return a success response.

    fi
    
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Checking environment variables from ${env_file}...${NC}"
    echo ""
    
    local missing_vars=0
    local total_vars=0
    local missing_list=()
    
    # Read .env.test and check each variable
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        # Skip empty lines and comments
        if [[ -z "$line" ]] || [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]]; then
            continue
        fi
        
        # Extract variable name (before =)
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)= ]]; then
            var_name="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            total_vars=$((total_vars + 1))
            
            # Check if variable is set and has a value
            if [ -z "${!var_name}" ]; then
                echo -e "${RED}✗ ${var_name} - NOT SET${NC}"
                missing_vars=$((missing_vars + 1))
                missing_list+=("$var_name")
            else
                echo -e "${GREEN}✓ ${var_name} - OK${NC}"
            fi
        fi
    done < "${env_file}"
    
    echo ""
    
    # Summary
    if [ $missing_vars -gt 0 ]; then
        echo -e "${RED}✗ Validation Failed!${NC}"
        echo "Missing ${missing_vars} out of ${total_vars} required environment variables:"
        for var in "${missing_list[@]}"; do
            echo "  - $var"
        done
        echo ""
        echo "Please set these variables before deploying."
        exit 1
    else
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ All ${total_vars} environment variables are set!${NC}"
        echo ""
    fi
}

# Function to send config to deployment orchestrator
send_config_to_orchestrator() {
    local env_file=".env.test"
    local orchestrator_url="http://localhost:47301/api/deploy-config"
    
    echo -e "${BLUE}=== Sending Config to Deployment Orchestrator ===${NC}"
    echo ""
    
    # Check if .env.test exists
    if [ ! -f "${env_file}" ]; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ Warning: ${env_file} not found. Skipping orchestrator submission.${NC}"
        echo ""
        return 0
    fi
    
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Building configuration JSON...${NC}"
    
    # Build JSON payload
    local json_payload="{"
    json_payload+="\"timestamp\":\"$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")\","
    json_payload+="\"project\":\"$(basename "$(pwd)")\","
    json_payload+="\"hostname\":\"$(hostname)\","
    json_payload+="\"user\":\"$(whoami)\","
    json_payload+="\"config\":{"
    
    local first_var=true
    
    # Read .env.test and build JSON with actual values
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        # Skip empty lines and comments
        if [[ -z "$line" ]] || [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]]; then
            continue
        fi
        
        # Extract variable name (before =)
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)= ]]; then
            var_name="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            var_value="${!var_name}"
            
            # Add comma separator for subsequent variables
            if [ "$first_var" = false ]; then
                json_payload+=","
            fi
            first_var=false
            
            # Escape special characters in JSON value
            var_value=$(echo "$var_value" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g; s/$/\\n/g' | tr -d '\n' | sed 's/\\n$//')
            
            json_payload+="\"${var_name}\":\"${var_value}\""
        fi
    done < "${env_file}"
    
    json_payload+="}}"
    
    echo "Submitting to: ${orchestrator_url}"
    echo ""
    
    # Send POST request to orchestrator
    response=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -X POST "${orchestrator_url}" \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d "${json_payload}" 2>&1)
    
    # Extract HTTP status code (last line)
    http_code=$(echo "$response" | tail -n1)
    # Extract response body (everything except last line)
    response_body=$(echo "$response" | sed '$d')
    
    # Check if curl command succeeded
    if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
        echo -e "${RED}✗ Failed to connect to deployment orchestrator${NC}"
        echo "Error: ${response}"
        echo ""
        echo "Please ensure the orchestrator is running at ${orchestrator_url}"
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Check HTTP status code
    if [ "$http_code" -ge 200 ] && [ "$http_code" -lt 300 ]; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Configuration submitted successfully${NC}"
        echo "Status: ${http_code}"
        if [ -n "$response_body" ]; then
            echo "Response: ${response_body}"
        fi
        echo ""
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ Failed to submit configuration${NC}"
        echo "Status: ${http_code}"
        if [ -n "$response_body" ]; then
            echo "Response: ${response_body}"
        fi
        echo ""
        echo "Deployment cannot proceed without audit compliance."
        exit 1
    fi
}

# Run validation
validate_env_vars

# Send config to orchestrator for audit compliance
send_config_to_orchestrator

echo -e "${BLUE}=== Creating Release Archive ===${NC}"
echo ""

# Get the current directory name for the archive
PROJECT_NAME=$(basename "$(pwd)")

# Generate timestamp for the release
TIMESTAMP=$(date +"%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")

# Archive filename
ARCHIVE_NAME="${PROJECT_NAME}_release_${TIMESTAMP}.tar.gz"

echo -e "${YELLOW}Creating release archive...${NC}"
echo "Project: ${PROJECT_NAME}"
echo "Archive: ${ARCHIVE_NAME}"
echo ""

# Create the archive excluding node_modules and .git
echo -e "${YELLOW}Compressing files...${NC}"
tar --exclude='node_modules' \
    --exclude='.git' \
    --exclude='*.tar.gz' \
    -czf "${ARCHIVE_NAME}" \
    -C .. \
    "$(basename "$(pwd)")"

# Check if archive was created successfully
if [ -f "${ARCHIVE_NAME}" ]; then
    ARCHIVE_SIZE=$(du -h "${ARCHIVE_NAME}" | cut -f1)
    echo ""
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Release archive created successfully!${NC}"
    echo "  File: ${ARCHIVE_NAME}"
    echo "  Size: ${ARCHIVE_SIZE}"
    echo ""
    echo "Excluded directories:"
    echo "  - node_modules/"
    echo "  - .git/"
    echo "  - *.tar.gz files"
else
    echo -e "${RED}✗ Failed to create release archive${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

# Deployment System Summary

## Overview
A complete deployment automation system with environment validation and audit compliance tracking.

## Components

### 1. deploy.sh (Main Deployment Script)
**Purpose:** Orchestrates the entire deployment process

**Features:**
- ✅ Validates all required environment variables from `.env.test`
- 📡 Sends validated config to orchestrator API for audit compliance
- 📦 Creates timestamped tar.gz release archives
- 🚫 Excludes node_modules, .git, and existing archives
- 🛡️ Comprehensive error handling and rollback on failure

**Usage:**
```bash
./deploy.sh
```

### 2. .env.test (Environment Configuration)
**Purpose:** Defines required environment variables for deployment

**Format:**
```bash
# Comments are allowed
VARIABLE_NAME=
ANOTHER_VAR=
```

**Notes:**
- Only variable names are listed (values come from shell environment)
- All listed variables must be set before deployment
- Empty lines and comments are ignored

### 3. mock_orchestrator.py (Test API Server)
**Purpose:** Simulates the deployment orchestrator API for testing

**Features:**
- Listens on port 47301
- Accepts POST requests to `/api/deploy-config`
- Logs all received configurations
- Masks sensitive values in console output
- Returns audit IDs for tracking

**Usage:**
```bash
./mock_orchestrator.py
```

**API Endpoint:**
```
POST http://localhost:47301/api/deploy-config
Content-Type: application/json
```

**Request Body:**
```json
{
  "timestamp": "2024-01-15T14:30:22Z",
  "project": "myproject",
  "hostname": "dev-machine",
  "user": "developer",
  "config": {
    "DATABASE_URL": "postgresql://localhost/db",
    "API_KEY": "secret-key"
  }
}
```

**Response:**
```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "message": "Configuration received and logged for audit compliance",
  "audit_id": "AUDIT-20240115143022",
  "variables_count": 2
}
```

### 4. test_deploy.sh (Automated Test)
**Purpose:** End-to-end testing of deployment workflow

**Features:**
- Sets up test environment variables
- Checks orchestrator availability
- Runs deployment script
- Reports success/failure with details

**Usage:**
```bash
./test_deploy.sh
```

### 5. QUICKSTART.sh (Quick Reference)
**Purpose:** Display quick start guide

**Usage:**
```bash
./QUICKSTART.sh
```

## Deployment Workflow

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         1. Pre-Deployment Validation        │
│  - Read .env.test                           │
│  - Check all variables are set              │
│  - Exit if any missing                      │
└────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│      2. Audit Compliance Submission         │
│  - Build JSON payload with all config       │
│  - POST to orchestrator API                 │
│  - Exit if submission fails                 │
└────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         3. Create Release Archive           │
│  - Generate timestamped filename            │
│  - Create tar.gz excluding specified dirs   │
│  - Verify archive created successfully      │
└────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            4. Deployment Complete           │
│  - Display archive information              │
│  - Exit with success                        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Error Handling

The script exits immediately on any failure:
- Missing environment variables → Exit code 1
- Orchestrator unreachable → Exit code 1
- Orchestrator returns error → Exit code 1
- Archive creation fails → Exit code 1

## Security Considerations

### What Gets Sent to Orchestrator
- ✅ All environment variable **values** (for audit trail)
- ✅ Deployment metadata (timestamp, user, hostname, project)

### Mock Orchestrator Security Features
- Masks sensitive values in console logs (SECRET, KEY, PASSWORD, TOKEN)
- Full values are still sent (simulating production behavior)

### Production Recommendations
1. Use HTTPS for orchestrator API
2. Implement authentication/authorization
3. Encrypt sensitive values in transit and at rest
4. Rotate audit logs regularly
5. Set up alerts for failed deployments

## File Exclusions

The following are automatically excluded from archives:
- `node_modules/` - Dependencies
- `.git/` - Git repository data
- `*.tar.gz` - Existing archives

## Testing Instructions

### Quick Test (Without Orchestrator)
```bash
# This will skip orchestrator submission
export DATABASE_URL="test"
export API_KEY="test"
./deploy.sh
```

### Full Test (With Orchestrator)
```bash

./mock_orchestrator.py

# Terminal 2
./test_deploy.sh
```

### Manual Test
```bash

./mock_orchestrator.py

# Terminal 2: Set variables and deploy

export DATABASE_NAME="mydb"
export DATABASE_USER="user"
export API_KEY="key123"
export API_SECRET="secret456"
export API_ENDPOINT="https://api.example.com"
export NODE_ENV="production"
export PORT="3000"
export AWS_REGION="us-east-1"
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="AKIA-IOSFODNN7EXAMPLE"
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY"

./deploy.sh
```

## Troubleshooting

### "Failed to connect to deployment orchestrator"
**Problem:** Orchestrator API is not running or unreachable

**Solution:**
```bash
# Start the mock orchestrator
./mock_orchestrator.py
```

### "Environment variable NOT SET"
**Problem:** Required variables are missing from shell environment

**Solution:**
```bash
# Export the missing variables
export VARIABLE_NAME="value"
```

### "Permission denied"
**Problem:** Scripts are not executable

**Solution:**
```bash
chmod +x deploy.sh mock_orchestrator.py test_deploy.sh QUICKSTART.sh
```

## Documentation Files

- `DEPLOY_README.md` - Comprehensive documentation with examples
- `SUMMARY.md` - This file - System overview
- `QUICKSTART.sh` - Quick reference guide

## Archive Naming Convention

Format: `{project}_release_{YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS}.tar.gz`

Example: `myproject_release_20240115_143022.tar.gz`

## Dependencies

- bash (4.0+)
- curl
- tar
- Python 3 (for mock orchestrator)

## Exit Codes

- `0` - Success
- `1` - Failure (validation, orchestrator, or archive creation)

---

**For detailed documentation, see:** `DEPLOY_README.md`  
**For quick reference, run:** `./QUICKSTART.sh`

#!/bin/bash

# Deployment script to create a release archive
# Excludes node_modules and .git directories

set -e  # Exit on error

# Color codes for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Get the current directory name for the archive
PROJECT_NAME=$(basename "$(pwd)")

# Generate timestamp for unique archive name
TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)

# Archive filename
ARCHIVE_NAME="${PROJECT_NAME}_release_${TIMESTAMP}.tar.gz"

echo -e "${YELLOW}Creating release archive...${NC}"
echo -e "Project: ${GREEN}${PROJECT_NAME}${NC}"
echo -e "Archive: ${GREEN}${ARCHIVE_NAME}${NC}"
echo ""

# Create the archive, excluding node_modules and .git
echo -e "${YELLOW}Packaging files...${NC}"
tar -czf "${ARCHIVE_NAME}" \
    --exclude='node_modules' \
    --exclude='.git' \
    --exclude='*.tar.gz' \
    --exclude='.gitignore' \
    --exclude='.DS_Store' \
    --exclude='*.log' \
    .

# Check if archive was created successfully
if [ -f "${ARCHIVE_NAME}" ]; then
    ARCHIVE_SIZE=$(du -h "${ARCHIVE_NAME}" | cut -f1)
    echo ""
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Release archive created successfully!${NC}"
    echo -e "Filename: ${GREEN}${ARCHIVE_NAME}${NC}"
    echo -e "Size: ${GREEN}${ARCHIVE_SIZE}${NC}"
    echo ""
    echo "Excluded directories/files:"
    echo "  - node_modules/"
    echo "  - .git/"
    echo "  - *.tar.gz"
    echo "  - .gitignore"
    echo "  - .DS_Store"
    echo "  - *.log"
else
    echo -e "${RED}✗ Failed to create release archive${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

set -e  # Exit on error

# Color codes for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Function to validate environment variables
validate_env_vars() {
    local env_file=".env.test"
    
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Validating environment variables...${NC}"
    
    # Check if .env.test exists
    if [ ! -f "${env_file}" ]; then
        echo -e "${RED}✗ ${env_file} not found!${NC}"
        echo -e "Please create ${env_file} with required environment variables."
        exit 1
    fi
    
    local missing_vars=()
    local empty_vars=()
    local valid_vars=0
    
    # Read .env.test and check each variable
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # Skip empty lines and comments
        [[ -z "$line" || "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
        
        # Extract variable name (before =)
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)[[:space:]]*= ]]; then
            var_name="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            
            # Get the value from current environment
            var_value="${!var_name}"
            
            if [ -z "${var_value}" ]; then
                # Check if it's defined but empty in .env.test
                if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*$ ]]; then
                    empty_vars+=("$var_name")
                else
                    missing_vars+=("$var_name")
                fi
            else
                valid_vars=$((valid_vars + 1))
            fi
        fi
    done < "${env_file}"
    
    # Report results
    echo ""
    if [ ${#missing_vars[@]} -eq 0 ] && [ ${#empty_vars[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ All ${valid_vars} required environment variables are set${NC}"
        echo ""
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ Environment validation failed!${NC}"
        echo ""
        
        if [ ${#missing_vars[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
            echo -e "${RED}Missing environment variables:${NC}"
            for var in "${missing_vars[@]}"; do
                echo -e "  - ${var}"
            done
            echo ""
        fi
        
        if [ ${#empty_vars[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
            echo -e "${RED}Empty environment variables in ${env_file}:${NC}"
            for var in "${empty_vars[@]}"; do
                echo -e "  - ${var}"
            done
            echo ""
        fi
        
        echo -e "${YELLOW}Please ensure all environment variables are set before deploying.${NC}"
        echo -e "You can set them by running: ${GREEN}export VAR_NAME=value${NC}"
        echo -e "Or source your .env file: ${GREEN}source .env${NC}"
        exit 1
    fi
}

# Deployment Script

This deployment script creates a release archive with pre-deployment validation.

## Features

### 1. Environment Variable Validation
- Reads `.env.test` to identify required environment variables
- Checks that all variables are set in the current environment
- Fails deployment if any required variables are missing or empty

### 2. Release Archive Creation
- Creates a timestamped tar.gz archive
- Excludes unnecessary files and directories
- Provides detailed output and archive information

## Usage

### Step 1: Configure Required Environment Variables

Edit `.env.test` to list all required environment variables:

```bash
# .env.test
DATABASE_URL=
API_KEY=
NODE_ENV=
```

### Step 2: Set Environment Variables

Before running the deployment script, ensure all variables are set:

```bash
# Option 1: Export individually
export DATABASE_URL="postgres://localhost/mydb"
export API_KEY="your-api-key"
export NODE_ENV="production"

# Option 2: Source from .env file
source .env
```

### Step 3: Run Deployment

```bash
./deploy.sh
```

## What Gets Excluded

The following files and directories are excluded from the archive:
- `node_modules/` - Node.js dependencies
- `.git/` - Git repository data
- `*.tar.gz` - Previous release archives
- `.gitignore` - Git configuration
- `.DS_Store` - macOS system files
- `*.log` - Log files

## Example Output

```

✓ All 12 required environment variables are set

Creating release archive...
Project: myproject
Archive: myproject_release_20240115_143022.tar.gz

Packaging files...

✓ Release archive created successfully!
Filename: myproject_release_20240115_143022.tar.gz
Size: 2.3M

Excluded directories/files:
  - node_modules/
  - .git/
  - *.tar.gz
  - .gitignore
  - .DS_Store
  - *.log
```

## Error Handling

If environment variables are missing, the script will fail with a helpful message:

```
✗ Environment validation failed!

Missing environment variables:
  - DATABASE_URL
  - API_KEY

Please ensure all environment variables are set before deploying.
You can set them by running: export VAR_NAME=value
Or source your .env file: source .env
```

## Customization

### Add More Exclusions

Edit the `tar` command in `deploy.sh`:

```bash
tar -czf "${ARCHIVE_NAME}" \
    --exclude='node_modules' \
    --exclude='.git' \
    --exclude='your-custom-exclusion' \
    .
```

### Change Environment File

Modify the `env_file` variable in the `validate_env_vars()` function:

```bash
local env_file=".env.production"  # Use different file
```

This guide shows how to test the deployment script with the mock orchestrator.

## Quick Test

# Set all environment variables

# Deployment System

A secure, audit-compliant deployment system that validates environment configuration and creates release archives.

## Overview

This deployment system provides:
- ✅ Environment variable validation
- 📋 Audit compliance via deployment orchestrator
- 📦 Automated release archive creation
- 🔒 Security through configuration verification

## Files

- **`deploy.sh`** - Main deployment script
- **`mock-orchestrator.js`** - Test server for orchestrator API
- **`.env.test`** - Template for required environment variables
- **`set-test-env.sh`** - Helper script to set test variables
- **`DEPLOYMENT.md`** - Complete deployment documentation
- **`TESTING.md`** - Testing guide and scenarios

## Quick Start

### 1. Setup Environment Variables

Option A: Source the test environment helper
```bash
source set-test-env.sh
```

Option B: Set your own variables
```bash
export DATABASE_URL="your-database-url"
export API_KEY="your-api-key"
# ... set all variables from .env.test
```

### 2. Start the Orchestrator (for testing)

```bash
node mock-orchestrator.js
```

### 3. Run Deployment

```bash
./deploy.sh
```

## How It Works

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  1. Validate Environment Variables          │
│     ├─ Read .env.test                       │
│     ├─ Check all vars are set               │
│     └─ Fail if any are missing              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                    ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  2. Send Config to Orchestrator (Audit)     │
│     ├─ Build JSON payload                   │
│     ├─ POST to orchestrator API             │
│     └─ Fail if rejected/unreachable         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                    ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  3. Create Release Archive                  │
│     ├─ Generate timestamped tar.gz          │
│     ├─ Exclude node_modules, .git, etc.     │
│     └─ Display archive details              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Configuration

### Required Environment Variables

Edit `.env.test` to define which variables are required:

```bash
# .env.test
DATABASE_URL=
API_KEY=
NODE_ENV=
```

All variables listed in `.env.test` must be set before deployment.

### Orchestrator URL

Default: `http://localhost:47301/api/deploy-config`

To change, edit `deploy.sh`:
```bash
local orchestrator_url="http://your-orchestrator/api/config"
```

## API Contract

### POST /api/deploy-config

**Request Body:**
```json
{
  "timestamp": "2024-01-15T14:30:22Z",
  "project": "myproject",
  "hostname": "dev-machine",
  "user": "developer",
  "config": {
    "DATABASE_URL": "postgres://localhost/mydb",
    "API_KEY": "your-api-key",
    "NODE_ENV": "production"
  }
}
```

**Success Response:** `200` or `201`
```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "message": "Configuration received and logged for audit",
  "audit_id": "AUDIT-1234567890"
}
```

**Error Response:** `4xx` or `5xx`
```json
{
  "error": "Validation failed",
  "message": "Configuration rejected"
}
```

## Security Notes

⚠️ **Important:** The deployment system sends actual environment variable values to the orchestrator for audit purposes. Ensure:

1. The orchestrator endpoint is secure (HTTPS in production)
2. The orchestrator properly logs and protects sensitive data
3. Network access to the orchestrator is restricted
4. Audit logs are encrypted and access-controlled

## Troubleshooting

### "curl is not installed"
```bash
# Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt-get install curl

# macOS
brew install curl
```

### "Failed to send configuration to orchestrator"
- Check if orchestrator is running: `curl http://localhost:47301/api/deploy-config`
- Verify network connectivity
- Check orchestrator logs for errors

### "Environment validation failed"
- List current env vars: `printenv | grep -E "(DATABASE|API|NODE|SMTP|APP)"`
- Source your .env file: `source .env` or `source set-test-env.sh`

## Documentation

- **[DEPLOYMENT.md](DEPLOYMENT.md)** - Complete deployment guide with examples
- **[TESTING.md](TESTING.md)** - Testing scenarios and procedures

## Example Usage

```bash
# Terminal 1: Start orchestrator
node mock-orchestrator.js

# Terminal 2: Deploy
source set-test-env.sh
./deploy.sh
```

# Deployment script to create a release archive
# Excludes node_modules and .git directories

set -e  # Exit on error

# Colors for output

GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Get the current directory name for the archive

# Generate timestamp for the archive name
TIMESTAMP=$(date +"%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")

echo ""

    --exclude='.DS_Store' \
    --exclude='*.log' \

# Deployment Script Usage

## Overview
The `deploy.sh` script creates a release archive of your project with pre-deployment validation.

## Features
- ✅ Validates all required environment variables before deployment
- ✅ Creates timestamped `.tar.gz` archives
- ✅ Excludes `node_modules`, `.git`, and other unnecessary files
- ✅ Color-coded output for easy reading
- ✅ Shows archive contents preview

## Setup

1. **Create `.env.test` file** with your required environment variables:
```bash
# .env.test
DATABASE_URL=
API_KEY=
NODE_ENV=
PORT=
```

2. **Set your environment variables** before running the script:
```bash
export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://localhost/mydb"
export API_KEY="your-api-key"
export NODE_ENV="production"
export PORT="3000"
```

Or source an existing `.env` file:
```bash
set -a
source .env
set +a
```

## Usage

```bash
./deploy.sh
```

## Example Output

### Success Case:
```
========================================
  Pre-Deployment Validation
========================================

Checking environment variables...
  ✓ DATABASE_URL: set
  ✓ API_KEY: set
  ✓ NODE_ENV: set
  ✓ PORT: set

✓ All environment variables validated successfully!

========================================
  Creating Release Archive
========================================

Building release package...
Project: myproject
Archive: myproject_release_20240115_143022.tar.gz

Packaging files...
✓ Release archive created successfully!
  File: myproject_release_20240115_143022.tar.gz
  Size: 1.2M

========================================
  Deployment Ready!
========================================
Archive ready for distribution: myproject_release_20240115_143022.tar.gz
```

### Failure Case (Missing Variables):
```
========================================
  Pre-Deployment Validation
========================================

Checking environment variables...
  ✓ DATABASE_URL: set
  ✗ API_KEY: NOT SET
  ✗ NODE_ENV: NOT SET
  ✓ PORT: set

========================================
  Validation Failed!
========================================

The following environment variables are missing:
  - API_KEY
  - NODE_ENV

Please set these variables before deployment:
  export VAR_NAME=value
  or source your .env file
```

## Customization

### Change the validation file
Edit the `ENV_TEST_FILE` variable in the script:
```bash
ENV_TEST_FILE=".env.production"
```

### Add more exclusions
Add to the `tar` command in the script:
```bash
tar -czf "$ARCHIVE_NAME" \
    --exclude='node_modules' \
    --exclude='.git' \
    --exclude='your-custom-exclusion' \
    .
```

## Notes
- The script uses `set -e` to exit immediately if any command fails
- Empty values in environment variables are treated as missing
- Comments and empty lines in `.env.test` are ignored
- Archives are created in the current directory with timestamp

#!/bin/bash

# Deployment script to create a release archive
# Excludes node_modules and .git directories

set -e  # Exit on error

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Configuration
ENV_TEST_FILE=".env.test"

echo -e "${BLUE}========================================${NC}"
echo -e "${BLUE}  Pre-Deployment Validation${NC}"
echo -e "${BLUE}========================================${NC}"
echo ""

# Validate environment variables
echo -e "${YELLOW}Checking environment variables...${NC}"

if [ ! -f "$ENV_TEST_FILE" ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}✗ Error: ${ENV_TEST_FILE} not found${NC}"
    echo -e "  Please create ${ENV_TEST_FILE} with required environment variables"
    exit 1
fi

# Read .env.test and validate each variable
VALIDATION_FAILED=0
MISSING_VARS=()
EMPTY_VARS=()

while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
    # Skip empty lines and comments
    if [[ -z "$line" ]] || [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]]; then
        continue
    fi
    
    # Extract the variable name (before the = sign)
    if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)[[:space:]]*= ]]; then
        VAR_NAME="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        
        # Get the value from current environment
        VAR_VALUE="${!VAR_NAME}"
        
        if [ -z "$VAR_VALUE" ]; then
            echo -e "  ${RED}✗${NC} ${VAR_NAME}: ${RED}NOT SET${NC}"
            MISSING_VARS+=("$VAR_NAME")
            VALIDATION_FAILED=1
        else
            echo -e "  ${GREEN}✓${NC} ${VAR_NAME}: set"
        fi
    fi
done < "$ENV_TEST_FILE"

echo ""

if [ $VALIDATION_FAILED -eq 1 ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}========================================${NC}"
    echo -e "${RED}  Validation Failed!${NC}"
    echo -e "${RED}========================================${NC}"
    echo ""
    echo -e "${RED}The following environment variables are missing:${NC}"
    for var in "${MISSING_VARS[@]}"; do
        echo -e "  - ${var}"
    done
    echo ""
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Please set these variables before deployment:${NC}"
    echo -e "  export VAR_NAME=value"
    echo -e "  or source your .env file"
    echo ""
    exit 1
fi

echo -e "${GREEN}✓ All environment variables validated successfully!${NC}"
echo ""

# Send validated config to deployment orchestrator
echo -e "${BLUE}========================================${NC}"
echo -e "${BLUE}  Sending Config to Orchestrator${NC}"
echo -e "${BLUE}========================================${NC}"
echo ""

ORCHESTRATOR_URL="http://localhost:47301/api/deploy-config"
echo -e "${YELLOW}Preparing configuration for audit...${NC}"

# Build JSON payload with all environment variables
JSON_PAYLOAD="{"
JSON_PAYLOAD+="\"timestamp\":\"$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")\","
JSON_PAYLOAD+="\"project\":\"$(basename "$PWD")\","
JSON_PAYLOAD+="\"environment_variables\":{"

FIRST_VAR=true
while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
    # Skip empty lines and comments
    if [[ -z "$line" ]] || [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]]; then
        continue
    fi
    
    # Extract the variable name and value
    if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)[[:space:]]*= ]]; then
        VAR_NAME="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        VAR_VALUE="${!VAR_NAME}"
        
        # Escape special characters in the value for JSON
        VAR_VALUE_ESCAPED=$(echo "$VAR_VALUE" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g' | sed 's/"/\\"/g' | sed 's/$/\\n/' | tr -d '\n' | sed 's/\\n$//')
        
        if [ "$FIRST_VAR" = true ]; then
            FIRST_VAR=false
        else
            JSON_PAYLOAD+=","
        fi
        
        JSON_PAYLOAD+="\"$VAR_NAME\":\"$VAR_VALUE_ESCAPED\""
    fi
done < "$ENV_TEST_FILE"

JSON_PAYLOAD+="},"
JSON_PAYLOAD+="\"env_file\":\"$ENV_TEST_FILE\","
JSON_PAYLOAD+="\"validation_status\":\"passed\""
JSON_PAYLOAD+="}"

echo -e "${YELLOW}Sending to orchestrator: ${ORCHESTRATOR_URL}${NC}"

# Send POST request to orchestrator
HTTP_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -X POST "$ORCHESTRATOR_URL" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "$JSON_PAYLOAD" 2>&1)

HTTP_CODE=$(echo "$HTTP_RESPONSE" | tail -n1)
HTTP_BODY=$(echo "$HTTP_RESPONSE" | sed '$d')

if [ "$HTTP_CODE" = "200" ] || [ "$HTTP_CODE" = "201" ]; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Configuration sent successfully (HTTP $HTTP_CODE)${NC}"
    echo -e "${GREEN}  Response: $HTTP_BODY${NC}"
else
    echo -e "${RED}✗ Failed to send configuration to orchestrator${NC}"
    echo -e "${RED}  HTTP Status: $HTTP_CODE${NC}"
    echo -e "${RED}  Response: $HTTP_BODY${NC}"
    echo ""
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Deployment cannot proceed without audit compliance.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

echo ""

# Get the current directory name for the archive
PROJECT_NAME=$(basename "$PWD")

# Generate timestamp for the archive name
TIMESTAMP=$(date +"%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")

# Archive filename
ARCHIVE_NAME="${PROJECT_NAME}_release_${TIMESTAMP}.tar.gz"

echo -e "${BLUE}========================================${NC}"
echo -e "${BLUE}  Creating Release Archive${NC}"
echo -e "${BLUE}========================================${NC}"
echo ""
echo -e "${YELLOW}Building release package...${NC}"
echo -e "Project: ${GREEN}${PROJECT_NAME}${NC}"
echo -e "Archive: ${GREEN}${ARCHIVE_NAME}${NC}"
echo ""

# Create the archive, excluding node_modules and .git
echo -e "${YELLOW}Packaging files...${NC}"
tar -czf "$ARCHIVE_NAME" \
    --exclude='node_modules' \
    --exclude='.git' \
    --exclude='*.tar.gz' \
    --exclude='.DS_Store' \
    --exclude='*.log' \
    .

# Check if archive was created successfully
if [ -f "$ARCHIVE_NAME" ]; then
    ARCHIVE_SIZE=$(du -h "$ARCHIVE_NAME" | cut -f1)
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Release archive created successfully!${NC}"
    echo -e "  File: ${ARCHIVE_NAME}"
    echo -e "  Size: ${ARCHIVE_SIZE}"
    echo ""
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Contents:${NC}"
    tar -tzf "$ARCHIVE_NAME" | head -20
    TOTAL_FILES=$(tar -tzf "$ARCHIVE_NAME" | wc -l)
    if [ "$TOTAL_FILES" -gt 20 ]; then
        echo -e "  ... and $((TOTAL_FILES - 20)) more files"
    fi
    echo ""
    echo -e "${GREEN}========================================${NC}"
    echo -e "${GREEN}  Deployment Ready!${NC}"
    echo -e "${GREEN}========================================${NC}"
    echo -e "${GREEN}Archive ready for distribution: ${ARCHIVE_NAME}${NC}"
else
    echo -e "${RED}✗ Failed to create archive${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

input.content:
#!/bin/bash

# Deployment script to create a release archive
# Excludes node_modules and .git directories

set -e  # Exit on error

# Configuration
TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)
PROJECT_NAME=$(basename "$(pwd)")
ARCHIVE_NAME="${PROJECT_NAME}_release_${TIMESTAMP}.tar.gz"
RELEASE_DIR="releases"

# Colors for output
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
RED='\033[0;31m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

echo -e "${BLUE}===========================================${NC}"
echo -e "${BLUE}   Creating Release Archive${NC}"
echo -e "${BLUE}===========================================${NC}"
echo ""

# Create releases directory if it doesn't exist
if [ ! -d "$RELEASE_DIR" ]; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}Creating releases directory...${NC}"
    mkdir -p "$RELEASE_DIR"
fi

# Create the archive
echo -e "${GREEN}Creating archive: ${ARCHIVE_NAME}${NC}"
echo -e "${GREEN}Excluding: node_modules, .git, releases${NC}"
echo ""

tar -czf "${RELEASE_DIR}/${ARCHIVE_NAME}" \
    --exclude='node_modules' \
    --exclude='.git' \
    --exclude='releases' \
    --exclude='*.tar.gz' \
    --exclude='.env' \
    --exclude='.DS_Store' \
    --exclude='*.log' \
    .

# Check if archive was created successfully
if [ -f "${RELEASE_DIR}/${ARCHIVE_NAME}" ]; then
    ARCHIVE_SIZE=$(du -h "${RELEASE_DIR}/${ARCHIVE_NAME}" | cut -f1)
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Archive created successfully!${NC}"
    echo ""
    echo -e "${BLUE}Archive Details:${NC}"
    echo -e "  Name: ${ARCHIVE_NAME}"
    echo -e "  Location: ${RELEASE_DIR}/${ARCHIVE_NAME}"
    echo -e "  Size: ${ARCHIVE_SIZE}"
    echo ""
    echo -e "${GREEN}===========================================${NC}"
    echo -e "${GREEN}   Deployment archive ready!${NC}"
    echo -e "${GREEN}===========================================${NC}"
else
    echo -e "${RED}✗ Error: Failed to create archive${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

# .env.test

export DATABASE_URL="postgres://localhost/mydb"

export NODE_ENV="production"
export PORT="3000"

# Listens on http://localhost:47301/api/deploy-config

        # Read until empty line (end of headers)
        if [ -z "$line" ] || [ "$line" = $'\r' ]; then

        fi
        
        # Capture Content-Length
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^Content-Length:\ ([0-9]+) ]]; then
            CONTENT_LENGTH="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        fi
    done

    # Read the POST body

        echo -e "$RESPONSE"
    fi
}

"""
Mock Deployment Orchestrator
A simple HTTP server for testing the deployment script
Listens on http://localhost:47301/api/deploy-config
"""

import json
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from http.server import HTTPServer, BaseHTTPRequestHandler

PORT = 47301
LOG_FILE = "orchestrator_audit.log"


class DeployConfigHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, format, *args):
        """Override to customize logging"""
        timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
        sys.stdout.write(f"[{timestamp}] {format % args}\n")

    def do_POST(self):
        """Handle POST requests to /api/deploy-config"""
        if self.path != '/api/deploy-config':
            self.send_error(404, "Not Found")
            return

        # Read the request body
        content_length = int(self.headers.get('Content-Length', 0))
        body = self.rfile.read(content_length).decode('utf-8')

        try:
            # Parse JSON
            config_data = json.loads(body)
            
            # Generate audit ID
            timestamp = datetime.now()
            audit_id = f"deploy-{timestamp.strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}"
            
            # Log to file
            with open(LOG_FILE, 'a') as f:
                f.write(f"\n{'='*60}\n")
                f.write(f"Timestamp: {timestamp.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\n")
                f.write(f"Audit ID: {audit_id}\n")
                f.write(f"Configuration:\n")
                f.write(json.dumps(config_data, indent=2))
                f.write(f"\n{'='*60}\n\n")
            
            # Console output
            print(f"✓ Config received and logged")
            print(f"  Audit ID: {audit_id}")
            print(f"  Variables: {len(config_data)}")
            
            # Send success response
            response = {
                "status": "accepted",
                "audit_id": audit_id,
                "timestamp": timestamp.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'),
                "variables_count": len(config_data)
            }
            
            self.send_response(200)
            self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(json.dumps(response).encode('utf-8'))
            
        except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
            # Invalid JSON
            error_response = {
                "status": "error",
                "message": f"Invalid JSON: {str(e)}"
            }
            self.send_response(400)
            self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(json.dumps(error_response).encode('utf-8'))
            print(f"✗ Error: Invalid JSON received")

    def do_GET(self):
        """Handle GET requests - return server info"""
        if self.path == '/health' or self.path == '/':
            response = {
                "status": "running",
                "service": "Mock Deployment Orchestrator",
                "endpoint": "/api/deploy-config",
                "method": "POST"
            }
            self.send_response(200)
            self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(json.dumps(response, indent=2).encode('utf-8'))
        else:
            self.send_error(404, "Not Found")


def run_server():
    """Start the HTTP server"""
    server_address = ('', PORT)
    httpd = HTTPServer(server_address, DeployConfigHandler)
    
    print("=" * 60)
    print("  Mock Deployment Orchestrator")
    print("=" * 60)
    print(f"\nServer running on http://localhost:{PORT}")
    print(f"Endpoint: POST http://localhost:{PORT}/api/deploy-config")
    print(f"Health check: GET http://localhost:{PORT}/health")
    print(f"Audit log: {LOG_FILE}")
    print("\nPress Ctrl+C to stop\n")
    
    try:
        httpd.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\n\nShutting down server...")
        httpd.shutdown()
        print("Server stopped.")


if __name__ == '__main__':
    run_server()

This directory contains a complete deployment system with audit compliance for environment configuration.

```

### 2. Start Mock Orchestrator (for testing)

```

### 3. Run Deployment

```bash
./deploy.sh
```

## Production Use

### Prerequisites

1. **Create `.env.test`** with your required variables:
   ```
   DATABASE_URL=
   API_KEY=
   SECRET_KEY=
   APP_ENV=
   ```

2. **Set environment variables** in your shell or CI/CD:
   ```bash
   export DATABASE_URL="postgres://prod-db/myapp"
   export API_KEY="prod-api-key"
   export SECRET_KEY="prod-secret"
   export APP_ENV="production"
   ```

3. **Configure orchestrator URL** in `deploy.sh`:
   ```bash
   ORCHESTRATOR_URL="https://your-orchestrator.company.com/api/deploy-config"
   ```

### Running in Production

```bash
./deploy.sh
```

The script will:
1. ✓ Validate all environment variables are set
2. ✓ Send config to orchestrator for audit trail
3. ✓ Create release archive in `releases/` directory
4. ✓ Report success or failure

## Workflow Diagram

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  1. Read .env.test                          │
│     Get list of required variables          │
└──────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                   │
                   ▼

│  2. Validate Environment                    │
│     Check each variable is set              │
│     ✓ All set → Continue                    │

└──────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                   │
                   ▼

```

## Security Notes

- **Sensitive Data**: The orchestrator receives actual environment values
- **Localhost Only**: Default config sends to localhost:47301
- **Audit Logs**: All configs are logged for compliance
- **No Secrets in Repo**: Never commit `.env` files or actual secrets
- **Production**: Use HTTPS for production orchestrator endpoints

## Audit Compliance

The system ensures audit compliance by:
1. **Mandatory Validation**: Cannot deploy without all required variables
2. **Configuration Logging**: All configs sent to orchestrator before deployment
3. **Audit Trail**: Orchestrator logs include timestamps and audit IDs
4. **Deployment Blocking**: Deployment fails if orchestrator is unreachable
5. **Traceable Releases**: Archives are timestamped and stored

## Troubleshooting

### "orchestrator_audit.log not found"
→ The mock orchestrator hasn't received any requests yet

### "Failed to send configuration (HTTP 000)"
→ Orchestrator is not running. Start with `./mock_orchestrator.py`

### "Variable X is not set or is empty"
→ Set the variable: `export X="value"` or run `./test_setup.sh`

### "Permission denied"
→ Make scripts executable: `chmod +x *.sh *.py`

import json

class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):

        pass
    def do_POST(self):
        if self.path == '/api/deploy-config':

            body = self.rfile.read(content_length).decode('utf-8')
            config_data = json.loads(body)

            print(f'Received config with {len(config_data)} variables', file=sys.stderr)

#!/bin/bash

# Deployment script to create a release archive
# Excludes node_modules and .git directories

set -e  # Exit on error

# Configuration
TIMESTAMP=$(date +"%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
PROJECT_NAME=$(basename "$PWD")
ARCHIVE_NAME="${PROJECT_NAME}_release_${TIMESTAMP}.tar.gz"
RELEASE_DIR="releases"

# Colors for output
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

echo -e "${BLUE}========================================${NC}"
echo -e "${BLUE}Creating Release Archive${NC}"
echo -e "${BLUE}========================================${NC}"
echo ""

# Create releases directory if it doesn't exist
if [ ! -d "$RELEASE_DIR" ]; then
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Creating releases directory...${NC}"
    mkdir -p "$RELEASE_DIR"
fi

echo -e "${BLUE}Project:${NC} $PROJECT_NAME"
echo -e "${BLUE}Archive:${NC} $ARCHIVE_NAME"
echo -e "${BLUE}Destination:${NC} $RELEASE_DIR/$ARCHIVE_NAME"
echo ""

# Create the archive
echo -e "${YELLOW}Creating archive (excluding node_modules and .git)...${NC}"
tar --exclude='node_modules' \
    --exclude='.git' \
    --exclude="$RELEASE_DIR" \
    --exclude='*.tar.gz' \
    -czf "$RELEASE_DIR/$ARCHIVE_NAME" \
    -C .. \
    "$(basename "$PWD")"

# Check if archive was created successfully
if [ -f "$RELEASE_DIR/$ARCHIVE_NAME" ]; then
    ARCHIVE_SIZE=$(du -h "$RELEASE_DIR/$ARCHIVE_NAME" | cut -f1)
    echo ""
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Archive created successfully!${NC}"
    echo -e "${GREEN}  Location: $RELEASE_DIR/$ARCHIVE_NAME${NC}"
    echo -e "${GREEN}  Size: $ARCHIVE_SIZE${NC}"
    echo ""
    
    # List contents of archive
    echo -e "${BLUE}Archive contents:${NC}"
    tar -tzf "$RELEASE_DIR/$ARCHIVE_NAME" | head -20
    
    TOTAL_FILES=$(tar -tzf "$RELEASE_DIR/$ARCHIVE_NAME" | wc -l)
    if [ "$TOTAL_FILES" -gt 20 ]; then
        echo "... and $((TOTAL_FILES - 20)) more files"
    fi
    
    echo ""
    echo -e "${GREEN}Deployment archive ready!${NC}"
else
    echo -e "${RED}✗ Failed to create archive${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

echo -e "${BLUE}========================================${NC}"

#!/bin/bash

# Deployment script to create a release archive
# Excludes node_modules and .git directories

set -e  # Exit on error

# Configuration
TIMESTAMP=$(date +"%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
PROJECT_NAME=$(basename "$PWD")
ARCHIVE_NAME="${PROJECT_NAME}_release_${TIMESTAMP}.tar.gz"
RELEASE_DIR="releases"
ENV_TEST_FILE=".env.test"

# Colors for output
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
RED='\033[0;31m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

echo -e "${BLUE}========================================${NC}"
echo -e "${BLUE}Creating Release Archive${NC}"
echo -e "${BLUE}========================================${NC}"
echo ""

# Pre-deployment validation
echo -e "${YELLOW}Running pre-deployment validation...${NC}"
echo ""

# Check if .env.test exists
if [ ! -f "$ENV_TEST_FILE" ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}✗ Error: $ENV_TEST_FILE not found${NC}"
    echo -e "${RED}  Please create $ENV_TEST_FILE with required environment variables${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

echo -e "${BLUE}Validating environment variables from $ENV_TEST_FILE...${NC}"

# Read .env.test and validate each variable
VALIDATION_FAILED=0
MISSING_VARS=()

while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
    # Skip empty lines and comments
    if [[ -z "$line" || "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]]; then
        continue
    fi
    
    # Extract variable name (before =)
    if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)= ]]; then
        VAR_NAME="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        
        # Extract value (after =)
        VAR_VALUE=$(echo "$line" | cut -d'=' -f2- | sed -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//' -e 's/^["'"'"']//' -e 's/["'"'"']$//')
        
        # Check if variable has a value
        if [ -z "$VAR_VALUE" ]; then
            echo -e "${RED}  ✗ $VAR_NAME - NOT SET${NC}"
            MISSING_VARS+=("$VAR_NAME")
            VALIDATION_FAILED=1
        else
            # Mask sensitive values in output (show only first 3 chars)
            MASKED_VALUE="${VAR_VALUE:0:3}***"
            echo -e "${GREEN}  ✓ $VAR_NAME - OK${NC} (${MASKED_VALUE})"
        fi
    fi
done < "$ENV_TEST_FILE"

echo ""

# Exit if validation failed
if [ $VALIDATION_FAILED -eq 1 ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}✗ Validation failed!${NC}"
    echo -e "${RED}  The following environment variables are missing or empty:${NC}"
    for var in "${MISSING_VARS[@]}"; do
        echo -e "${RED}    - $var${NC}"
    done
    echo ""
    echo -e "${YELLOW}  Please set all required environment variables in $ENV_TEST_FILE${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

echo -e "${GREEN}✓ All environment variables validated successfully!${NC}"
echo ""
